Traveling to New York City with teenagers requires a tricky balance: you need a hotel with enough **space and comfort for parents**, but with a **cool vibe, fast Wi-Fi, and a great location for teens** who want to explore.

Here are the top hotel recommendations in Midtown Manhattan for families with teenagers, broken down by what makes them special:

---

### 1. Best Overall for Teens: **Hard Rock Hotel New York**
* **Location:** Music Row (48th St between 6th & 7th Ave) — Steps from Times Square and Rockefeller Center.
* **Why Teens Will Love It:** It has a high "cool factor." The design is sleek and music-focused, featuring memorabilia from artists like Taylor Swift and Lady Gaga. Teens can even order a **Fender guitar delivered to their room** with headphones to practice.
* **Why Parents Will Love It:** It's brand new (opened 2022), extremely clean, and surprisingly well-soundproofed against the city noise outside.
* **Room Setup:** Offers rooms with two queen beds (rare for boutique NYC hotels) and spacious suites.

### 2. Best for Space, Views & Value: **Residence Inn Manhattan / Central Park**
* **Location:** 54th St & 8th Ave (Near Central Park and Broadway).
* **Why Teens Will Love It:** It is located in the **tallest hotel building in North America**. Request a high floor for insane floor-to-ceiling views of Central Park or the city skyline (major Instagram points). 
* **Why Parents Will Love It:** 
  * **Free hot breakfast daily** (a massive money-saver with hungry teenagers).
  * Rooms feature **kitchenettes** with mini-fridges and microwaves for late-night snacks.
* **Room Setup:** Studio suites with two double beds plus a pull-out sofa, giving everyone room to spread out.

### 3. Best for Fun Amenities: **Margaritaville Resort Times Square**
* **Location:** 40th St & 7th Ave (South end of Times Square, near Bryant Park).
* **Why Teens Will Love It:** It features the **only outdoor heated pool in Midtown** that is open year-round. The tropical vibe feels like a vacation within a vacation, and it's surrounded by bustling shops.
* **Why Parents Will Love It:** It’s surprisingly quiet inside despite being right in the action. Bryant Park is just two blocks away, offering a nice escape from the heavy Times Square crowds.
* **Room Setup:** Modern rooms with double queen options and great city views.

### 4. Best Boutique & Tech-Forward: **LUMA Hotel Times Square**
* **Location:** 41st St between 5th & 6th Ave (Overlooking Bryant Park).
* **Why Teens Will Love It:** LUMA has **"ALEXA," a robot butler** that delivers extra towels, snacks, and amenities directly to your guest room door. It’s super modern with high-speed Wi-Fi and streaming-ready TVs.
* **Why Parents Will Love It:** It is on a quieter side street right off Bryant Park, making it feel safer and less chaotic at night. Excellent service and complimentary wine hours for adults.
* **Room Setup:** Family rooms feature two king beds (unheard of in NYC) or two queen beds with smart layouts.

### 5. Best Classic & Dependable: **The Westin New York at Times Square**
* **Location:** 42nd St & 8th Ave.
* **Why Teens Will Love It:** Direct underground access to the subway (A/C/E lines), making it super easy to head downtown to Soho, Greenwich Village, or Brooklyn for shopping and food tours.
* **Why Parents Will Love It:** The hotel is massive and accustomed to families. The rooms are significantly larger than the NYC average, and their "Heavenly Beds" ensure everyone actually gets sleep.
* **Room Setup:** Traditional two-double or two-queen bed options, plus connecting room configurations upon request.

---

### Quick Decision Guide:
* Choose **Residence Inn** if you want to save money on food (free breakfast) and want extra space.
* Choose **Hard Rock Hotel** if your teens care about aesthetics, trendiness, and music.
* Choose **Margaritaville** if your teens want to swim and hang out by a pool.
* Choose **LUMA** if you want a quieter, higher-end boutique experience right next to Bryant Park.

**Pro-Tip for NYC with Teens:** Always check the bed sizes carefully when booking! Many NYC hotels list "Double" beds instead of "Queens," which can be tight for two growing teenagers sharing a bed. Look specifically for **Two Queen** or **Suite** options.

* Choose **LUMA** if you want a quieter, higher-end boutique experience right next to Bryant Park.

Assuming you are looking in **Midtown Manhattan, New York City**, the top recommendation for a private celebration is **The Refinery Hotel** (specifically for its rooftop venue, **Refinery Rooftop**). 

Here is why it stands out, along with a few alternative options tailored to different vibes for your celebration.

---

### **Top Pick: Refinery Hotel (Refinery Rooftop)**
* **Location:** 63 W 38th St (Midtown South / Garment District)
* **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, sophisticated yet accessible.
* **The View:** Unobstructed, direct views of the Empire State Building.
* **Why it’s ideal for a private celebration:**
  * **All-Weather Advantage:** It features a **retractable glass roof**, meaning your event goes on rain, shine, or snow without sacrificing the skyline view.
  * **Flexible Event Spaces:** Offers full rooftop buyouts, semi-private lounge areas, or indoor/outdoor sections depending on your guest count.
  * **Food & Beverage:** Known for high-end craft cocktails and excellent elevated tavern-style food packages.

---

### **Alternative Options Depending on Your Vibe**

#### **1. For Ultra-Luxury & Elegance: The Peninsula New York (*Salon de Ning*)**
* **Location:** 700 5th Ave (Midtown East)
* **The Vibe:** High-end, classic Manhattan glamour with Asian-inspired chic decor.
* **The View:** Sweeping views looking right down Fifth Avenue.
* **Best For:** Milestone anniversaries, formal private cocktail receptions, or high-budget celebrations requiring white-glove service.
* **Highlights:** Features two outdoor terraces and an intimate indoor bar area.

#### **2. For an Intimate & View-Centric Party: Archer Hotel (*Spyglass Rooftop Bar*)**
* **Location:** 45 W 38th St (Midtown)
* **The Vibe:** 1940s/50s glam, intimate, upscale.
* **The View:** Dramatic, close-up, straight-on view of the Empire State Building.
* **Best For:** Small-to-medium groups (up to 50–75 people) wanting a stylish, photogenic space with top-tier craft cocktails.

#### **3. For a High-Energy, Trendy Party: Moxy NYC Times Square (*Magic Hour Rooftop Lounge*)**
* **Location:** 485 7th Ave (Midtown West)
* **The Vibe:** Playful, vibrant, and sprawling.
* **The View:** Empire State Building views with a whimsical, "urban amusement park" aesthetic (complete with a miniature golf course and carousel seating).
* **Best For:** Big birthday parties or high-energy celebrations. It is NYC's largest all-season hotel rooftop venue, offering multiple distinct zones for private rent.

---

### **Tips for Booking a Rooftop Private Event in Midtown:**
1. **Inquire Early:** Rooftop spaces in Midtown are in high demand, especially during May–June and September–October.
2. **Ask About F&B Minimums:** Most hotel rooftops charge a Food & Beverage minimum for private buyouts rather than a flat venue fee.
3. **Check the Weather Contingency:** If choosing an open-air rooftop, always confirm their indoor back-up space or tenting options (which is why **Refinery Hotel**'s retractable glass roof is such a safe bet).

To make a graduation celebration weekend in New York City feel special, you want a hotel that offers a great mix of location, celebratory atmosphere, excellent dining or rooftop options, and comfortable rooms for families or groups.

Here are the top hotel recommendations near Broadway, categorized by style and vibe:

---

### 1. The Ultimate Trendy Luxury: **The Times Square EDITION**
* **Location:** 701 7th Ave (at 47th St) — Right in the heart of the Theater District.
* **Vibe:** Chic, sophisticated, and elevated. It feels worlds away from the chaos of Times Square once you walk inside.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:** 
  * Features **The Terrace and Outdoor Gardens**, a gorgeous restaurant led by Michelin-starred Chef John Fraser.
  * Has stunning views of the city skyline and Times Square.
  * Perfect for a celebratory cocktail before heading to a Broadway show.

### 2. For Theater Lovers & Boutique Charm: **CIVILIAN Hotel**
* **Location:** 305 W 48th St (between 8th & 9th Aves) — A quiet, historic block in Hell’s Kitchen, steps from Broadway.
* **Vibe:** Artsy, stylish, and curated specifically as a love letter to Broadway theater.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * Designed by David Rockwell, featuring stage-set style elements and curated Broadway memorabilia.
  * **Starchild Rooftop Bar** offers amazing views and a fantastic celebration venue.
  * Excellent ground-floor restaurant (**Rosevale Kitchen**) and piano bar for a festive night in.

### 3. Best for Families Needing Extra Space: **Conrad New York Midtown**
* **Location:** 151 W 54th St — A few blocks north of the main theater strip, closer to Central Park and MoMA.
* **Vibe:** Quiet luxury, spacious, and upscale.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * It is an **all-suite hotel**, meaning the rooms are massive compared to standard NYC sizes—ideal if parents, siblings, or friends are sharing space.
  * Features modern luxury amenities and a calm atmosphere to relax in after a long day of walking.
  * **DABBLE** (the hotel’s lounge) is great for celebratory drinks and light bites.

### 4. Historic Elegance & Great Rooftop: **The Knickerbocker Hotel**
* **Location:** 6 Central Park South / 142 W 42nd St (corner of Broadway & 42nd).
* **Vibe:** Classic NYC history meets modern luxury.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * Home to **St. Cloud**, one of the best rooftop bars overlooking Times Square—an unforgettable spot for a celebratory toast.
  * High-ceilinged, soundproofed rooms mean you get the central location without the noise.
  * Walking distance to almost every major Broadway theater and Bryant Park.

### 5. High-End Boutique Value: **LUMA Hotel Times Square**
* **Location:** 120 W 41st St (between 6th Ave & Broadway, near Bryant Park).
* **Vibe:** Modern, intimate, and detail-oriented.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * Consistently rated as having some of the best customer service in Midtown.
  * Offers complimentary evening sangria hours in the lobby.
  * On-site Basque restaurant, **AperiBar** by Chef Charlie Palmer, is fantastic for a pre-show celebration dinner.

---

### Pro-Tips for a Graduation Weekend in NYC:

1. **Inform the Hotel in Advance:** When booking (or calling ahead), make sure to mention you are celebrating a graduation. Many of these hotels will place a complimentary bottle of sparkling wine, dessert, or a welcome note in the room.
2. **Make Dinner Reservations NOW:** Pre-theater dining (5:00 PM – 6:30 PM) fills up weeks in advance in the Theater District. Recommended nearby celebration spots:
   * **Joe Allen** (Classic Broadway hangout, 46th St)
   * **Hunt & Fish Club** (Upscale steakhouse, 44th St)
   * **Bond 45** (Italian, great for group celebrations, 46th St)
3. **Broadway Tickets:** If you're seeing a show, book well ahead, or use the **TodayTix** app for digital rush options if you’re flexible.

Hosting a bachelorette party in the Times Square area puts you right in the heart of NYC’s energy. The secret to a great Times Square bachelorette is choosing venues that offer high-end, memorable experiences while avoiding overly crowded tourist traps. 

By venturing just a few blocks into **Hell’s Kitchen** (just west of Times Square) or **Koreatown** (a 10-minute walk south), you can expand your options significantly.

Here are the best spots to host a bachelorette party in and around Times Square, broken down by vibe:

---

### 1. The Ultimate "Instagrammable" Rooftops
*If you want pink cocktails, stunning views, and great photo ops:*

*   **Magic Hour Rooftop Bar & Lounge (at the Moxy Times Square):** This is practically built for bachelorette parties. It features an "urban amusement park" theme, complete with a pink carousel, miniature golf, over-the-top cocktails, and epic views of the Empire State Building. 
*   **St. Cloud Rooftop (at The Knickerbocker Hotel):** Located right on the corner of 42nd and Broadway, this offers a luxury, high-end vibe. It features private corner sky pods overlooking Times Square—great if you want something sophisticated rather than wild.
*   **Castell Rooftop Lounge:** Located on the 21st floor of the AC Hotel (40th St), this is a chic, cozy cocktail lounge with a warm fireplace, outdoor terrace, and fantastic martinis.

---

### 2. Fun Group Dinners
*Spots that easily accommodate large parties and have high energy:*

*   **Legasea Seafood Brasserie:** Also inside the Moxy Times Square, this trendy seafood spot has a vibrant atmosphere, fun group dining menus, and a festive "party dinner" vibe.
*   **Boqueria (AC Hotel / 40th St):** Perfect for groups who like to share. This lively Spanish tapas bar serves amazing sangria pitchers, churros, and small plates.
*   **Carmine’s (44th St):** A Times Square institution. If you have a huge group and want family-style Italian food with giant portions and cheap-per-person pricing, this is the classic choice.
*   **Bond 45:** A massive Italian steakhouse near Broadway that is great for large groups. *Bonus:* It features a secret, cool speakeasy downstairs called **Downstairs at Bond** for post-dinner drinks.

---

### 3. Entertainment & Nightlife
*For sing-alongs, dancing, and unique activities:*

*   **Lips Drag Queen Show (Hell's Kitchen - 10 min walk):** The undisputed king of NYC bachelorette parties. They offer themed dinner shows, bottomless drag brunches, and hilarious performances that put the bride front and center.
*   **Don’t Tell Mama (46th St):** A legendary piano bar and cabaret space in the heart of the Theater District. The bartenders and waitstaff are Broadway-level singers who take requests for epic sing-alongs.
*   **Koreatown Private Karaoke (32nd St - 10 min walk south):** Walk a few blocks south to "K-Town" and book a private room at **GAGOPA Karaoke** or **Spot Karaoke**. You can order drinks/food directly to your private suite and sing all night.
*   **Swingers Crazy Golf (NoMad - 5 min cab ride):** An upscale, adults-only indoor mini-golf venue with street food vendors, multiple bars, and a 1920s English country clubhouse theme.

---

### 4. Daytime & Boozy Brunch
*To kick off the day:*

*   **Sugar Factory (39th St):** Known for giant, smoking candy-infused "goblet" cocktails, over-the-top milkshakes, and neon decor. It’s loud, sugary, and very festive for a bride with a sweet tooth.
*   **Pink Taco (39th St):** Right around the corner from Times Square, offering pink margaritas, upbeat music, colorful tacos, and a loud, fun brunch/lunch atmosphere.
*   **The Pink Elephant Brunch at Magic Hour:** Magic Hour’s weekend brunch features pink pancakes, giant cocktail towers, and a DJ set.

---

### Pro-Tips for Planning in Midtown:
1. **Book Reservations 30–60 Days Out:** NYC venues fill up fast, especially for groups larger than 6. 
2. **Utilize "Hell's Kitchen":** For late-night bar hopping, walk West past 8th Avenue into Hell's Kitchen. The bars along 9th and 10th Avenues are less touristy, very LGBTQ+-friendly, and full of local energy.
3. **Check Dress Codes:** Places like Magic Hour and St. Cloud enforce strict dress codes (especially for footwear and party attire/props like sashes—call ahead to make sure bride gear is allowed).

When it comes to experiencing New Year’s Eve in New York City with luxury, comfort, and prime access to the Ball Drop, staying at a hotel inside the security perimeter of Times Square is essential. This allows you to bypass the freezing crowds on the street while enjoying VIP parties, fine dining, and private room views.

Here are the **top upscale hotels** near the Ball Drop, ranked by luxury level, view potential, and NYE experience:

---

### 1. The Knickerbocker Hotel (The Ultimate #1 Pick)
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Historic Luxury
* **Location:** Corner of 42nd St & Broadway (Literally directly below the Ball)
* **The NYE Experience:** The Knickerbocker sits just **150 feet below the Times Square Ball**. Its famous rooftop bar, *St. Cloud*, hosts one of the most exclusive, high-end NYE galas in the world. You can watch the ball drop live from the outdoor terrace with a glass of champagne in hand, completely elevated above the street crowds.
* **Best For:** Guests who want the absolute closest, most iconic view of the Ball Drop in a refined, historic setting.

### 2. The Times Square EDITION
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Modern & Trendy Luxury
* **Location:** 701 7th Avenue (47th St & 7th Ave)
* **The NYE Experience:** Created by boutique hotel legend Ian Schrager, the EDITION offers sophisticated luxury right in the heart of the action. Select higher-floor suites offer direct views of the Ball Drop. They throw a high-profile, ultra-stylish NYE party featuring Michelin-starred dining from Chef John Fraser, live entertainment, and open bars.
* **Best For:** Younger luxury travelers, design lovers, and those seeking a chic, celebrity-favorite party vibe.

### 3. The Chatwal, New York
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Art Deco & Bespoke Service
* **Location:** 130 West 44th Street (Half a block from Times Square)
* **The NYE Experience:** If you want luxury *without* being situated directly inside the loud chaos, The Chatwal is the answer. Located just steps off Broadway, this historic landmark offers personal butler service and classic NYC elegance. While room views of the drop are limited, the hotel provides police passes for effortless walking access to Times Square, plus a world-class multi-course NYE dinner at *The Lambs Club*.
* **Best For:** Travelers seeking discreet, quiet luxury, top-tier service, and a cozy haven away from the madness.

### 4. New York Marriott Marquis
* **Luxury Level:** 4.5-Star / Modern Classic
* **Location:** 1535 Broadway (45th St & Broadway)
* **The NYE Experience:** This is the giant anchor of Times Square. While it is a larger, busier hotel than the Knickerbocker or EDITION, its location is unbeatable. Many of its high-floor rooms and suites face directly toward the Ball. They host a massive VIP NYE party inside the *Broadway Lounge*, which features floor-to-ceiling glass windows with a direct, warm, indoor view of the main stage and Ball Drop.
* **Best For:** Guaranteed panoramic indoor views of the Ball Drop without having to step outside into the cold.

### 5. Hyatt Centric Times Square New York
* **Luxury Level:** 4.5-Star / Upscale Lifestyle
* **Location:** 135 West 45th Street
* **The NYE Experience:** Home to **Bar 54**, one of the highest open-air hotel rooftop lounges in NYC. Sitting 54 stories up, the rooftop party offers staggering, unobstructed views of the city skyline and a direct line-of-sight to the Times Square Ball Drop. 
* **Best For:** Unmatched high-altitude views and a lively rooftop lounge scene.

---

### 💡 Crucial Tips for Booking NYE in Times Square:

1. **Book a "Ball Drop View" Specific Room:** Standard rooms at these hotels often face interior courtyards or side streets. If you want to watch the drop from your room, you must explicitly book a category that guarantees a *Ball Drop View* (these often require direct phone inquiries or special NYE booking packages).
2. **Minimum Stay Requirements:** Almost all upscale hotels in the perimeter enforce a **3- to 5-night minimum stay** over the New Year's holiday.
3. **Street Security Access:** On December 31, the NYPD locks down Times Square. Your hotel will issue you physical passes/credentials so you can pass through police barricades to reach your hotel lobby.
4. **Budget Realities:** Expect room rates for NYE view-packages to range from **$2,000 to $10,000+ per night**, with rooftop gala tickets costing between **$1,000 and $3,000+ per person**. 

**Verdict:** If you want the absolute best overall experience combining top-tier luxury, history, and a direct view of the drop, book **The Knickerbocker Hotel**.

* **Location:** Corner of 42nd St & Broadway (Literally directly below the Ball)

You can watch the ball drop live from the outdoor terrace with a glass of champagne in hand, completely elevated above the street crowds.
* **Best For:** Guests who want the absolute closest, most iconic view of the Ball Drop in a refined, historic setting.

### 2. The Times Square EDITION
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Modern & Trendy Luxury
* **Location:** 701 7th Avenue (47th St & 7th Ave)
* **The NYE Experience:** Created by boutique hotel legend Ian Schrager, the EDITION offers sophisticated luxury right in the heart of the action. Select higher-floor suites offer direct views of the Ball Drop. They throw a high-profile, ultra-stylish NYE party featuring Michelin-starred dining from Chef John Fraser, live entertainment, and open bars.
* **Best For:** Younger luxury travelers, design lovers, and those seeking a chic, celebrity-favorite party vibe.

### 3. The Chatwal, New York
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Art Deco & Bespoke Service
* **Location:** 130 West 44th Street (Half a block from Times Square)
* **The NYE Experience:** If you want luxury *without* being situated directly inside the loud chaos, The Chatwal is the answer. Located just steps off Broadway, this historic landmark offers personal butler service and classic NYC elegance. While room views of the drop are limited, the hotel provides police passes for effortless walking access to Times Square, plus a world-class multi-course NYE dinner at *The Lambs Club*.
* **Best For:** Travelers seeking discreet, quiet luxury, top-tier service, and a cozy haven away from the madness.

### 4. New York Marriott Marquis
* **Luxury Level:** 4.5-Star / Modern Classic
* **Location:** 1535 Broadway (45th St & Broadway)
* **The NYE Experience:** This is the giant anchor of Times Square. While it is a larger, busier hotel than the Knickerbocker or EDITION, its location is unbeatable. They host a massive VIP NYE party inside the *Broadway Lounge*, which features floor-to-ceiling glass windows with a direct, warm, indoor view of the main stage and Ball Drop.

* **Location:** 135 West 45th Street
* **The NYE Experience:** Home to **Bar 54**, one of the highest open-air hotel rooftop lounges in NYC. Sitting 54 stories up, the rooftop party offers staggering, unobstructed views of the city skyline and a direct line-of-sight to the Times Square Ball Drop.

### 💡 Crucial Tips for Booking NYE in Times Square:

If you want to watch the drop from your room, you must explicitly book a category that guarantees a *Ball Drop View* (these often require direct phone inquiries or special NYE booking packages).
2. **Minimum Stay Requirements:** Almost all upscale hotels in the perimeter enforce a **3- to 5-night minimum stay** over the New Year's holiday.

* **Location:** 305 W 48th St (between 8th & 9th Aves) — A quiet, historic block in Hell’s Kitchen, steps from Broadway.

* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * Designed by David Rockwell, featuring stage-set style elements and curated Broadway memorabilia.
  * **Starchild Rooftop Bar** offers amazing views and a fantastic celebration venue.
  * Excellent ground-floor restaurant (**Rosevale Kitchen**) and piano bar for a festive night in.

### 3. Best for Families Needing Extra Space: **Conrad New York Midtown**
* **Location:** 151 W 54th St — A few blocks north of the main theater strip, closer to Central Park and MoMA.
* **Vibe:** Quiet luxury, spacious, and upscale.
* **Why it’s great for graduation:**
  * It is an **all-suite hotel**, meaning the rooms are massive compared to standard NYC sizes—ideal if parents, siblings, or friends are sharing space.
  * Features modern luxury amenities and a calm atmosphere to relax in after a long day of walking.
  * **DABBLE** (the hotel’s lounge) is great for celebratory drinks and light bites.

  * Home to **St. Cloud**, one of the best rooftop bars overlooking Times Square—an unforgettable spot for a celebratory toast.
  * High-ceilinged, soundproofed rooms mean you get the central location without the noise.

  * Consistently rated as having some of the best customer service in Midtown.

---

### 1. The Best Overall (Luxury & High-Energy Chic): **The Times Square EDITION**
If you want an upscale, glamorous birthday with incredible design, famous dining, and nightlife all under one roof, this is the top pick. It feels like a private oasis floating right above the craziness of Times Square.
* **The Vibe:** Trendy luxury, sophisticated, and exclusive.
* **Birthday Highlights:** 
  * **Terrace Outdoor Gardens:** A lush, green restaurant overlooking Times Square.
  * **Paradise Club:** An intimate, high-end nightlife venue/cabaret inside the hotel.
  * **The Rooms:** Sleek, minimalist rooms with floor-to-ceiling windows offering sweeping views of the billboards.

### 2. Best for a Fun, Party Vibe: **Moxy NYC Times Square**
If you are celebrating with a group of friends and want a youthful, social atmosphere with a massive rooftop scene, book the Moxy. 
* **The Vibe:** Playful, trendy, energetic, and social media-friendly.
* **Birthday Highlights:** 
  * **Magic Hour Rooftop Bar & Lounge:** NYC’s largest all-season indoor/outdoor hotel rooftop, featuring an amusement-park theme, custom cocktails, and unbeatable views of the Empire State Building.
  * **Dining:** Home to *Legasea*, a lively seafood brasserie great for group dinners.
* *Note:* Standard rooms are on the smaller "micro-luxury" side, so consider booking a suite if you want space to get ready with friends.

### 3. Best for the Highest Rooftop Views: **Hyatt Centric Times Square New York**
If your dream birthday involves sipping champagne while looking out over the NYC skyline from extreme heights, this is your spot.
* **The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, and central.
* **Birthday Highlights:** 
  * **Bar 54:** Located on the 54th floor, this is the highest open-air hotel rooftop bar in New York City. The sunset and nighttime views are dramatic and perfect for birthday photos.
  * **Location:** Tucked slightly off the main strip on 45th Street, giving you quick access to the action without being overwhelmed the second you step out the front door.

### 4. Best for Sophisticated / Milestone Luxury: **The Chatwal**
If you are celebrating a major milestone (30th, 40th, 50th) and prefer timeless elegance, personalized service, and a quieter street just steps from Broadway, choose The Chatwal.
* **The Vibe:** 1930s Art Deco luxury, romantic, and upscale.
* **Birthday Highlights:** 
  * **Butler Service:** Personal butler service is available to handle birthday details, champagne drop-offs, and reservations.
  * **The Lambs Club:** A legendary, stylish restaurant and lounge with a massive fireplace, perfect for a cozy, fancy birthday dinner or cocktail.

### 5. Best Classic Times Square Experience: **New York Marriott Marquis**
If you want to be right in the literal heart of Times Square with iconic views, massive spaces, and classic NYC energy.
* **The Vibe:** Grand, bustling, and immersive.
* **Birthday Highlights:** 
  * **Glass Elevators:** Soaring up the atrium sets a fun, dramatic tone.
  * **Revel & Rye / Broadway Lounge:** Offers massive floor-to-ceiling windows hanging directly over the neon lights of Broadway. 
  * **Location:** You are steps away from every major Broadway theater.

---

### 💡 Pro-Tips for a Birthday Stay in Times Square:

1. **Notify the Hotel in Advance:** When booking (and at check-in), make sure to mention you are celebrating a birthday. Luxury hotels like *The EDITION* or *The Chatwal* will often send up a complimentary bottle of bubbly, dessert, or a room upgrade if available.
2. **Book Rooftop Reservations Early:** Popular hotel bars like *Magic Hour* (Moxy) and *Bar 54* (Hyatt Centric) fill up weeks in advance, especially on weekends. Secure table reservations when you book your room.
3. **Ask for a High Floor:** Times Square is bright and loud 24/7. Request a room on a higher floor (20+) to reduce street noise while maximizing the lights and view.

- **Margaritaville Times Square** — At 560 7th Ave.; a relaxed, high-energy setting for private dinners, cocktails, celebrations, and group gatherings.[3]
- **Marriott Marquis / Broadway Lounge** — A more polished choice for larger groups, with private-event and buyout options in the heart of Times Square.[5]
- **Ever One Times Square** — A distinctive option for a smaller, more intimate celebration, with spaces for approximately 4–75 guests and views directly over Times Square.[7]

- **Most fun:** Lucky Strike  
- **Best rooftop:** The Skylark  
- **Best casual dinner:** Virgil’s  
- **Best for a large group:** Marriott Marquis  
- **Most uniquely “Times Square”:** Ever One Times Square

* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Modern & Trendy Luxury

* **The NYE Experience:** Created by boutique hotel legend Ian Schrager, the EDITION offers sophisticated luxury right in the heart of the action. * **Best For:** Younger luxury travelers, design lovers, and those seeking a chic, celebrity-favorite party vibe.

### 3. The Chatwal, New York
* **Luxury Level:** 5-Star / Art Deco & Bespoke Service
* **Location:** 130 West 44th Street (Half a block from Times Square)
* **The NYE Experience:** If you want luxury *without* being situated directly inside the loud chaos, The Chatwal is the answer. Located just steps off Broadway, this historic landmark offers personal butler service and classic NYC elegance. While room views of the drop are limited, the hotel provides police passes for effortless walking access to Times Square, plus a world-class multi-course NYE dinner at *The Lambs Club*.
* **Best For:** Travelers seeking discreet, quiet luxury, top-tier service, and a cozy haven away from the madness.

### 4. New York Marriott Marquis
* **Luxury Level:** 4.5-Star / Modern Classic
* **Location:** 1535 Broadway (45th St & Broadway)
* **The NYE Experience:** This is the giant anchor of Times Square. While it is a larger, busier hotel than the Knickerbocker or EDITION, its location is unbeatable. Many of its high-floor rooms and suites face directly toward the Ball. They host a massive VIP NYE party inside the *Broadway Lounge*, which features floor-to-ceiling glass windows with a direct, warm, indoor view of the main stage and Ball Drop.
* **Best For:** Guaranteed panoramic indoor views of the Ball Drop without having to step outside into the cold.

### 5. Hyatt Centric Times Square New York
* **Luxury Level:** 4.5-Star / Upscale Lifestyle
* **Location:** 135 West 45th Street
* **The NYE Experience:** Home to **Bar 54**, one of the highest open-air hotel rooftop lounges in NYC. Sitting 54 stories up, the rooftop party offers staggering, unobstructed views of the city skyline and a direct line-of-sight to the Times Square Ball Drop. 
* **Best For:** Unmatched high-altitude views and a lively rooftop lounge scene.

---

**Verdict:** If you want the absolute best overall experience combining top-tier luxury, history, and a direct view of the drop, book **The Knickerbocker Hotel**.

Assuming you are looking in **Midtown Manhattan, New York City**, the top recommendation for a private celebration is **The Refinery Hotel** (specifically for its rooftop venue, **Refinery Rooftop**). 

Here is why it stands out, along with a few alternative options tailored to different vibes for your celebration.

---

### **Top Pick: Refinery Hotel (Refinery Rooftop)**
* **Location:** 63 W 38th St (Midtown South / Garment District)
* **The Vibe:** Industrial-chic, sophisticated yet accessible.
* **The View:** Unobstructed, direct views of the Empire State Building.
* **Why it’s ideal for a private celebration:**
  * **All-Weather Advantage:** It features a **retractable glass roof**, meaning your event goes on rain, shine, or snow without sacrificing the skyline view.
  * **Flexible Event Spaces:** Offers full rooftop buyouts, semi-private lounge areas, or indoor/outdoor sections depending on your guest count.
  * **Food & Beverage:** Known for high-end craft cocktails and excellent elevated tavern-style food packages.

---

### **Alternative Options Depending on Your Vibe**

#### **1. For Ultra-Luxury & Elegance: The Peninsula New York (*Salon de Ning*)**
* **Location:** 700 5th Ave (Midtown East)
* **The Vibe:** High-end, classic Manhattan glamour with Asian-inspired chic decor.
* **The View:** Sweeping views looking right down Fifth Avenue.
* **Best For:** Milestone anniversaries, formal private cocktail receptions, or high-budget celebrations requiring white-glove service.
* **Highlights:** Features two outdoor terraces and an intimate indoor bar area.

#### **2. For an Intimate & View-Centric Party: Archer Hotel (*Spyglass Rooftop Bar*)**
* **Location:** 45 W 38th St (Midtown)
* **The Vibe:** 1940s/50s glam, intimate, upscale.
* **The View:** Dramatic, close-up, straight-on view of the Empire State Building.
* **Best For:** Small-to-medium groups (up to 50–75 people) wanting a stylish, photogenic space with top-tier craft cocktails.

#### **3. For a High-Energy, Trendy Party: Moxy NYC Times Square (*Magic Hour Rooftop Lounge*)**
* **Location:** 485 7th Ave (Midtown West)
* **The Vibe:** Playful, vibrant, and sprawling.
* **The View:** Empire State Building views with a whimsical, "urban amusement park" aesthetic (complete with a miniature golf course and carousel seating).
* **Best For:** Big birthday parties or high-energy celebrations. It is NYC's largest all-season hotel rooftop venue, offering multiple distinct zones for private rent.

---

### **Tips for Booking a Rooftop Private Event in Midtown:**
1. **Inquire Early:** Rooftop spaces in Midtown are in high demand, especially during May–June and September–October.
2. **Ask About F&B Minimums:** Most hotel rooftops charge a Food & Beverage minimum for private buyouts rather than a flat venue fee.
3. **Check the Weather Contingency:** If choosing an open-air rooftop, always confirm their indoor back-up space or tenting options (which is why **Refinery Hotel**'s retractable glass roof is such a safe bet).

evidence.aiResponse:
While several hotels claim the title, the absolute **best hotel in Midtown Manhattan for spa and wellness** is **Aman New York**. 

However, depending on whether your definition of "wellness" leans toward **ultra-luxury relaxation, high-performance fitness, or boutique pampering**, a few top-tier contenders stand out. 

Here is the breakdown of the best options in Midtown:

---

### 1. The Undisputed King of Luxury & Spa: **Aman New York**
* **Location:** 57th St & 5th Ave (Midtown East/Central Park South)
* **Vibe:** Ultra-exclusive, serene, zen-like sanctuary.
* **The Wellness Experience:** The **Aman Spa** spans three full floors (nearly 25,000 square feet) and is arguably the most impressive urban spa in North America. 
* **Key Features:**
  * A 65-foot indoor swimming pool lined with daybeds and fire pits.
  * Two private **Spa Houses** featuring a double treatment room, sauna and steam rooms, and a private outdoor terrace with hot and cold plunge pools.
  * Cryotherapy chambers, a yoga/Pilates studio, and a state-of-the-art fitness center.
  * **Best For:** Travelers wanting total isolation, bespoke wellness programs, and unlimited budget for luxury.

---

### 2. Best for High-Performance Fitness & Biohacking: **Equinox Hotel Hudson Yards**
* **Location:** 33rd St & 10th Ave (Midtown West / Hudson Yards)
* **Vibe:** Sleek, modern, science-backed athletic luxury.
* **The Wellness Experience:** Built entirely around the philosophy of "movement, nutrition, and regeneration," this hotel treats sleep and recovery as a science.
* **Key Features:**
  * Access to the 60,000 sq. ft. Flagship Equinox Club.
  * **The Spa at Equinox:** Offers cryotherapy, infrared saunas, quantum harmonics massage, bodywork, and IV drip therapy.
  * Outdoor heated pool and sun deck overlooking the Hudson River, plus a indoor lap pool.
  * Rooms (called "Dark, Quiet, Cool" sleep chambers) feature soundproofing, blackout shades, and temperature-regulating beds.
  * **Best For:** Athletes, fitness enthusiasts, and travelers looking to optimize energy and recover from jet lag.

---

### 3. Best for Glamour & Skincare: **Baccarat Hotel New York**
* **Location:** 53rd St between 5th & 6th Ave (Midtown)
* **Vibe:** Opulent French luxury, crystal chandeliers, ultra-chic.
* **The Wellness Experience:** Houses the **Spa de La Mer**—the first dedicated spa in the United States by the legendary high-end skincare brand, La Mer.
* **Key Features:**
  * Custom facial and body treatments using La Mer’s signature Miracle Broth™.
  * A stunning, checkered-tile indoor pool surrounded by plush daybeds that evoke the French Riviera.
  * Intimate, highly personalized, and quiet atmosphere.
  * **Best For:** Skincare obsessives, couples, and those looking for an intimate, luxurious pampering session.

---

### 4. Best Classic Luxury with Central Park Views: **Park Hyatt New York**
* **Location:** 57th St between 6th & 7th Ave (Midtown)
* **Vibe:** Modern, spacious, understated elegance.
* **The Wellness Experience:** Home to **Spa Nalai**, which focuses on personalized treatments based on holistic wellness pillars.
* **Key Features:**
  * A sunlit, 65-foot indoor hydrotherapy pool featuring underwater speakers playing a curated playlist from Carnegie Hall (located across the street).
  * Eucalyptus steam rooms and a oversized hot tub.
  * Direct views of Midtown from the pool and relaxation lounges.
  * **Best For:** Swimming lovers, business travelers needing to unwind, and lovers of modern, spacious hotel rooms.

---

### 5. Best Traditional Asian-Inspired Wellness: **The Peninsula New York**
* **Location:** 55th St & 5th Ave (Midtown East)
* **Vibe:** Old-world Fifth Avenue elegance and timeless service.
* **The Wellness Experience:** The **Peninsula Spa** occupies the top floors of the hotel, providing a quiet retreat high above Fifth Avenue with a strong emphasis on Ayurvedic and holistic treatments.
* **Key Features:**
  * Glass-enclosed indoor pool with city views and a seasonal outdoor sun deck.
  * Thermal suites including aromatherapy steam rooms, saunas, and ice fountains.
  * Asian-inspired holistic treatments, massage therapy, and mindfulness options.
  * **Best For:** Classic luxury lovers who want traditional, top-tier hotel spa service.

---

### Summary Recommendation:
* Choose **Aman New York** if you want the absolute highest-end, peaceful spa day money can buy.
* Choose **Equinox Hotel** if you care more about fitness, sauna/cold plunges, and modern biohacking than traditional pampering.
* Choose **Baccarat** if you want elite facials (La Mer) in a romantic, opulent setting.

For a food and theater enthusiast, the ideal hotel in Midtown sits in the **"sweet spot"**: walking distance to Broadway, but far enough from the chaotic core of Times Square to offer a tranquil, upscale sanctuary—and surrounded by exceptional dining.

Here are the top upscale Midtown hotels tailored specifically for your interests, ranging from stylish boutique luxury to classic opulence.

---

### 1. The Whitby Hotel (Upper Midtown / 56th St)
**The Vibe:** Whimsical, British-chic boutique luxury with world-class design.
* **Why for Theater:** Located on 56th Street between 5th and 6th Avenues, it’s a scenic 10-minute walk south to the Broadway theaters. It gives you immediate access to the shows without the street noise.
* **Why for Food:** **The Whitby Bar & Restaurant** is a neighborhood destination for elevated British/American cuisine and one of the best Afternoon Teas in the city. You are also steps away from NYC fine-dining royalty like **Le Bernardin** (3 Michelin stars), **The Modern** (at MoMA), and **Marea**.
* **Bonus:** They have an in-house, 130-seat state-of-the-art screening room that often hosts cultural events.

### 2. The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel (44th St)
**The Vibe:** Art Deco glamour steeped in Broadway history.
* **Why for Theater:** Located right in the heart of the Theater District on 44th Street, you can walk out the door and be at your seat in under 3 minutes. The building itself was originally designed by Stanford White in 1905 as the home of *The Lambs*, America’s first professional theatrical club. 
* **Why for Food:** It houses **The Lambs Club**, a classic, red-leather-booth mahogany dining room ideal for a high-end pre-theater dinner or a late-night nightcap. You’re also close to the eclectic dining corridor of Hell's Kitchen (9th Avenue).
* **Bonus:** Exceptional butler service to help secure last-minute house seats or hard-to-get dining reservations.

### 3. The Times Square EDITION (47th St & 7th Ave)
**The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, high-fashion luxury floating above the neon.
* **Why for Theater:** Right at the northern edge of Times Square. Once inside, the lush, plant-filled oasis completely insulates you from the street level. You are surrounded by every major Broadway house.
* **Why for Food:** The hotel’s culinary program is helmed by Michelin-starred chef **John Fraser**. **701 West** offers an exquisite, sophisticated fine-dining experience (with a incredible champagne cart), and **The Terrace** offers excellent, lighter pre-theater fair in a stunning garden greenhouse setting.
* **Bonus:** The hotel’s venue, **Paradise Club**, hosts elevated, avant-garde cabaret and nightlife performances right on site.

### 4. The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue (36th St & 5th Ave)
**The Vibe:** Polished, contemporary luxury with some of the largest hotel rooms in Midtown.
* **Why for Theater:** Located slightly south on Fifth Avenue near Bryant Park, it’s a quick 12-to-15-minute walk to the Broadway houses (or a 3-minute taxi ride), positioning you near the theater action while feeling distinctly high-end.
* **Why for Food:** It features **Ai Fiori**, an acclaimed restaurant serving Riviera-inspired Mediterranean and Italian cuisine. Their handmade pasta and wine program are legendary, making it a dream for a luxurious pre-theater dinner. You are also near **Gabriel Kreuther** (2 Michelin stars) by Bryant Park.

### 5. Baccarat Hotel New York (53rd St)
**The Vibe:** Unapologetic French opulence, crystal elegance, and ultra-luxury service.
* **Why for Theater:** Located across from MoMA on 53rd Street, you are a quick 8-minute walk to the northern Broadway theaters (like *The Broadway Theatre* or *Winter Garden*) and a short cab ride to the rest.
* **Why for Food:** The food and beverage program is curated by Culinary Director Gabriel Kreuther. **The Grand Salon** serves incredible Alsatian-inspired fare on Baccarat crystal, and **The Bar** is famous for serving some of the best-crafted cocktails in Midtown in an incredible setting.

---

### Neighborhood & Dining Strategy Tip for Your Trip:
* **Pre-Theater Timing:** Broadway shows strictly start at 7:00 PM or 8:00 PM. Tell your restaurant server immediately that you have a "curtain time." For a full sit-down meal, aim for a **5:00 PM or 5:30 PM reservation**.
* **Post-Theater Bites:** For a late-night bite or dessert after the show, skip the tourist traps in Times Square and head to **Alderman** (upscale cocktail parlor/American), **Joe Allen** (a famous Broadway cast hangout), or **The Whitby Bar** for a nightcap.

For easy access to museums, Broadway, and restaurants in New York City, consider staying in the Midtown Manhattan area. This location provides a central base for exploring many of the city's cultural attractions. Here are a few neighborhoods and hotel suggestions:

1. **Theater District/Times Square**:
   - **Hotels**: The Westin New York at Times Square, The Times Square EDITION, or the InterContinental New York Times Square.
   - **Benefits**: Close proximity to Broadway theaters, numerous dining options, and a lively atmosphere.

2. **Midtown East**:
   - **Hotels**: The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue; Lotte New York Palace; or the Waldorf Astoria.
   - **Benefits**: Easy access to museums like the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA), and a short subway ride to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

3. **Upper West Side**:
   - **Hotels**: Hotel Beacon, The Lucerne Hotel, or NYLO New York City.
   - **Benefits**: Close to the American Museum of Natural History and Central Park, with a more residential feel and excellent dining options.

4. **Upper East Side**:
   - **Hotels**: The Mark, The Carlyle, A Rosewood Hotel, or The Surrey.
   - **Benefits**: Proximity to the “Museum Mile” which includes the Met, the Guggenheim, and the Neue Galerie.

5. **Chelsea/Flatiron**:
   - **Hotels**: The Moxy NYC Chelsea, Kimpton Hotel Eventi, or The NoMad Hotel.
   - **Benefits**: Known for art galleries, excellent dining options, and a vibrant nightlife, with easy access to Broadway via subway.

These areas are well-connected by public transportation, making it easy to explore other parts of the city as well. Always check for hotel deals and reviews to find the best fit for your needs and budget.

For a food and theater enthusiast, the ideal hotel in Midtown sits in the **"sweet spot"**: walking distance to Broadway, but far enough from the chaotic core of Times Square to offer a tranquil, upscale sanctuary—and surrounded by exceptional dining.

Here are the top upscale Midtown hotels tailored specifically for your interests, ranging from stylish boutique luxury to classic opulence.

---

### 1. The Whitby Hotel (Upper Midtown / 56th St)
**The Vibe:** Whimsical, British-chic boutique luxury with world-class design.
* **Why for Theater:** Located on 56th Street between 5th and 6th Avenues, it’s a scenic 10-minute walk south to the Broadway theaters. It gives you immediate access to the shows without the street noise.
* **Why for Food:** **The Whitby Bar & Restaurant** is a neighborhood destination for elevated British/American cuisine and one of the best Afternoon Teas in the city. You are also steps away from NYC fine-dining royalty like **Le Bernardin** (3 Michelin stars), **The Modern** (at MoMA), and **Marea**.
* **Bonus:** They have an in-house, 130-seat state-of-the-art screening room that often hosts cultural events.

### 2. The Chatwal, a Luxury Collection Hotel (44th St)
**The Vibe:** Art Deco glamour steeped in Broadway history.
* **Why for Theater:** Located right in the heart of the Theater District on 44th Street, you can walk out the door and be at your seat in under 3 minutes. The building itself was originally designed by Stanford White in 1905 as the home of *The Lambs*, America’s first professional theatrical club. 
* **Why for Food:** It houses **The Lambs Club**, a classic, red-leather-booth mahogany dining room ideal for a high-end pre-theater dinner or a late-night nightcap. You’re also close to the eclectic dining corridor of Hell's Kitchen (9th Avenue).
* **Bonus:** Exceptional butler service to help secure last-minute house seats or hard-to-get dining reservations.

### 3. The Times Square EDITION (47th St & 7th Ave)
**The Vibe:** Sleek, modern, high-fashion luxury floating above the neon.
* **Why for Theater:** Right at the northern edge of Times Square. Once inside, the lush, plant-filled oasis completely insulates you from the street level. You are surrounded by every major Broadway house.
* **Why for Food:** The hotel’s culinary program is helmed by Michelin-starred chef **John Fraser**. **701 West** offers an exquisite, sophisticated fine-dining experience (with a incredible champagne cart), and **The Terrace** offers excellent, lighter pre-theater fair in a stunning garden greenhouse setting.
* **Bonus:** The hotel’s venue, **Paradise Club**, hosts elevated, avant-garde cabaret and nightlife performances right on site.

### 4. The Langham, New York, Fifth Avenue (36th St & 5th Ave)
**The Vibe:** Polished, contemporary luxury with some of the largest hotel rooms in Midtown.
* **Why for Theater:** Located slightly south on Fifth Avenue near Bryant Park, it’s a quick 12-to-15-minute walk to the Broadway houses (or a 3-minute taxi ride), positioning you near the theater action while feeling distinctly high-end.
* **Why for Food:** It features **Ai Fiori**, an acclaimed restaurant serving Riviera-inspired Mediterranean and Italian cuisine. Their handmade pasta and wine program are legendary, making it a dream for a luxurious pre-theater dinner. You are also near **Gabriel Kreuther** (2 Michelin stars) by Bryant Park.

### 5. Baccarat Hotel New York (53rd St)
**The Vibe:** Unapologetic French opulence, crystal elegance, and ultra-luxury service.
* **Why for Theater:** Located across from MoMA on 53rd Street, you are a quick 8-minute walk to the northern Broadway theaters (like *The Broadway Theatre* or *Winter Garden*) and a short cab ride to the rest.
* **Why for Food:** The food and beverage program is curated by Culinary Director Gabriel Kreuther. **The Grand Salon** serves incredible Alsatian-inspired fare on Baccarat crystal, and **The Bar** is famous for serving some of the best-crafted cocktails in Midtown in an incredible setting.

---

### Neighborhood & Dining Strategy Tip for Your Trip:
* **Pre-Theater Timing:** Broadway shows strictly start at 7:00 PM or 8:00 PM. Tell your restaurant server immediately that you have a "curtain time." For a full sit-down meal, aim for a **5:00 PM or 5:30 PM reservation**.
* **Post-Theater Bites:** For a late-night bite or dessert after the show, skip the tourist traps in Times Square and head to **Alderman** (upscale cocktail parlor/American), **Joe Allen** (a famous Broadway cast hangout), or **The Whitby Bar** for a nightcap.
